title: Scientists Create Chocolate That Burns Calories
author: Sophie Reynolds
text:
Chocolate lovers may finally have an excuse to eat dessert
for breakfast. A new chocolate bar reportedly burns more
calories during digestion than it contains.

Its creators claim that a special combination of cocoa and
plant extracts forces the body to use extra energy while
processing the chocolate. Eating two bars daily could
supposedly help people lose weight without changing their diet.

The product is expected to reach supermarkets soon, although
the company has not released clinical trial results. Its
website currently accepts pre-orders for a limited time.
explanation:
FAKE! No clinical trials are given
to support the claim that
chocolate burns more calories than
it contains. The seller also
pushes pre-orders. Check health
claims before buying.

title: School Bans Homework After AI Study
author: Oliver Grant
text:
An Australian school has reportedly banned homework after an
AI-powered study found that students learn more by playing video
games. The school claims the decision has already improved results.

According to the report, researchers monitored students for
several weeks and discovered that gaming improved memory and
problem-solving skills more effectively than traditional homework.

The school's principal allegedly described the results as
revolutionary. However, neither the school nor the researchers
have been named, and the full study has not been published.
explanation:
FAKE! The article never names the
school or researchers, and the
study isn't available. Improving
some gaming skills does not prove
homework is useless. Look for the
original research.

title: Queensland Trees Reportedly Glow Before Rain
author: Daniel Mitchell
text:
Scientists in northern Queensland have reportedly discovered
an unusual eucalyptus tree that glows blue before rainfall.
The discovery was allegedly made during a wildlife survey,
when researchers noticed trees glowing before a thunderstorm.

According to the research team, rising humidity causes a
chemical reaction inside the leaves, producing a faint blue
light. Researchers claim the brighter the glow, the greater
the chance of rain within the following few hours.

Environmental groups are reportedly interested in using the
trees as natural weather-warning systems in remote areas.
However, the researchers have not yet released their full
findings. For now, your weather app is probably safe.
explanation:
FAKE! No scientists, institution
or published study are named. A
glowing tree is an unusual claim
that needs strong evidence.
Scientific-sounding words alone
aren't proof.

title: Octopuses Have Three Hearts and Blue Blood
author: Emily Carter
text:
Octopuses might look like creatures from another planet, but
what if their biology is even stranger? These eight-armed animals
have three hearts and blue blood. Apparently, eight arms weren't
enough to make them interesting!

Two hearts pump blood through their gills, while the third sends
oxygen-rich blood around the body. Their blood is blue because
it contains haemocyanin, a copper-based protein that carries
oxygen instead of the iron-based protein found in human blood.

Scientists have also observed octopuses solving puzzles, opening
containers and escaping from aquariums. Some can even recognise
individual humans. With three hearts and eight arms, perhaps
they're planning something we don't know about.
explanation:
TRUE! Three hearts and blue blood
sound strange, but the article
explains how they work. Check
marine biology references for
haemocyanin and the octopus
circulatory system.

title: AI Predicts Exact Date of Next Earthquake
author: Nathan Brooks
text:
A new artificial intelligence system has reportedly predicted
the exact date and location of a major earthquake. Its
developers claim the technology could save thousands of lives.

The system supposedly analyses underground vibrations,
weather patterns and historical earthquake records to predict
when dangerous movements will occur. Its creators say the
technology has already achieved perfect accuracy in testing.

Despite these claims, the developers have not released their
testing data or explained how independent scientists could
verify the predictions. A public demonstration is promised soon.
explanation:
FAKE! The developers claim perfect
accuracy but share no test
results. AI can analyse patterns,
but exact earthquake predictions
aren't established. Look for
independent testing.

title: New Phone App Can Translate Cat Thoughts
author: Mia Patterson
text:
Ever wondered what your cat thinks of you? A new smartphone
app reportedly uses artificial intelligence to translate
meows into complete English sentences.

Developers claim the app analyses thousands of recordings to
identify emotions and intentions. During a demonstration, one
cat supposedly told its owner that dinner was three minutes late.

The company says its software can translate more than 90%
of feline communication. However, no independent animal
behaviour researchers have confirmed these results.
explanation:
FAKE! The app claims over 90%
accuracy without explaining its
tests. Studying cat sounds isn't
the same as translating thoughts.
Check for independent animal
research.

title: Oxford Is Older Than the Aztec Empire
author: William Parker
text:
Oxford University in England is older than the Aztec Empire.
Although this might sound impossible, the historical dates
support the surprising comparison.

Teaching was taking place at Oxford by 1096, centuries before
the Aztec Empire emerged in the early 1400s. The Aztec capital,
Tenochtitlan, was founded in 1325.

Oxford did not begin as the modern university we recognise
today, but its teaching history stretches back further than
many famous civilisations and institutions.
explanation:
TRUE! The dates are checkable:
teaching at Oxford began by 1096,
before the Aztec Empire formed.
Compare reliable university and
history records rather than
guessing.

title: A Day on Venus Is Longer Than Its Year
author: Charlotte Reed
text:
Imagine celebrating your birthday before finishing a single
day. On Venus, this strange situation is possible because
the planet rotates extremely slowly.

Venus takes approximately 243 Earth days to complete one
rotation on its axis, but only about 225 Earth days to
travel around the Sun.

This means its rotation period is longer than its orbital
period. Venus also rotates in the opposite direction to
most planets, making its movements particularly unusual.
explanation:
TRUE! Venus takes about 243 Earth
days to rotate but about 225 to
orbit the Sun. NASA data can
verify both figures. Note that a
full rotation differs from sunrise
to sunrise.

title: Australian Beach Sand Found to Charge Phones
author: Liam Foster
text:
Researchers have reportedly discovered that sand from a
Queensland beach can generate enough electricity to charge
mobile phones when exposed to sunlight.

The unusual sand supposedly contains minerals that produce
an electrical current without requiring solar panels. A
research team claims that a small container of sand could
fully charge a smartphone in less than an hour.

The discovery could revolutionise renewable energy, according
to the article. However, the beach's location, research team
and experimental results have not been publicly identified.
explanation:
FAKE! The beach, researchers and
test results aren't identified.
The claim that sand charges phones
needs measurements and independent
experiments, not just a dramatic
headline.

title: Crows Remember Human Faces
author: Amelia Scott
text:
Crows may remember someone who has treated them badly, even
years after the encounter. Researchers have discovered that
these intelligent birds can recognise individual human faces.

In experiments, scientists wore distinctive masks while
capturing and releasing crows. Later, birds reacted more
strongly to people wearing the threatening masks.

The findings suggest crows can remember dangerous individuals
and may learn warning signals from other crows. So perhaps
it's best to stay on good terms with the neighbourhood birds.
explanation:
TRUE! The article describes a test
using masks, which readers can
investigate. Published crow
studies support face recognition.
Check the experiment rather than
dismissing the claim.

title: Students Only Use 10% of Their Brains
author: Grace Wilson
text:
A new report claims that most students use only 10% of their
brains during school lessons. Researchers allegedly believe
special concentration exercises could unlock the remaining 90%.

The report suggests that students who practise these exercises
could remember entire textbooks after reading them once. One
online course promises noticeable improvements within a week.

The article describes the technique as scientifically proven,
but provides no links to brain scans, published studies or
independent medical researchers.
explanation:
FAKE! The '10% of our brains' idea
is a myth. The article offers no
brain scans or studies and
promotes a memory course. Verify
the science with reliable
neuroscience sources.

title: Bananas Are Berries but Strawberries Aren't
author: Noah Evans
text:
Despite their names, bananas are classified as berries by
botanists, while strawberries are not. Apparently, fruit
has been ignoring our naming rules for centuries.

In botany, a berry develops from a flower's single ovary
and usually has seeds enclosed within its fleshy interior.
Bananas fit this botanical definition, even though most
commercial varieties have tiny, undeveloped seeds.

Strawberries develop differently and are classified as
aggregate accessory fruits. The small structures on their
surface are actually individual fruits.
explanation:
TRUE! Botanists classify fruit by
how it develops, not its everyday
name. Check botanical definitions:
bananas are berries, while
strawberries are accessory fruits.

title: Turtles Can Breathe Through Their Bottoms
author: Olivia Harris
text:
Some freshwater turtles have an unusual way of surviving
underwater: they can absorb oxygen through specialised
structures near their rear end.

This process, called cloacal respiration, allows certain
turtle species to obtain oxygen from water without surfacing
as frequently. It is particularly useful when they remain
underwater for extended periods.

However, turtles do not literally breathe through their
bottoms in the same way humans breathe through their lungs.
The process involves specialised tissues that absorb oxygen.
explanation:
TRUE! Some turtles absorb oxygen
through tissues near their rear
end. The article names cloacal
respiration and explains its
limits. Verify the process in
wildlife research.

title: Crime Drop After Removing Streetlights
author: Ethan Miller
text:
A city council has reportedly discovered that switching off
streetlights reduces crime. According to its report, recorded
crime fell by 30% after lights were removed from several streets.

Officials claim the darker streets discouraged criminals by
making it harder to see potential targets. The council is
considering expanding the trial to other neighbourhoods.

However, the article does not explain how many crimes occurred,
whether reporting changed or if other safety measures were
introduced during the same period.
explanation:
FAKE! The article gives a 30%
figure but names no city or
official dataset. Even a real drop
wouldn't prove darkness caused it.
Check the original numbers and
other explanations.

title: AI Image Shows Giant Shark Near Sydney Beach
author: Chloe Bennett
text:
An image circulating online appears to show an enormous shark
swimming just metres from swimmers at a Sydney beach. The
picture has attracted thousands of shares and worried comments.

The account that first posted the image claims the shark was
larger than a bus. Several users have demanded that local
beaches close immediately to protect swimmers.

However, the original photographer has not been identified,
and the post provides no date, location details or official
confirmation from lifeguards or marine authorities.
explanation:
FAKE! The dramatic image has no
identified photographer, exact
location or official confirmation.
Images can be AI-generated or
altered. Check trusted reports and
the image's origin.

title: Sharks Are Older Than Trees
author: Jack Thompson
text:
Sharks have been swimming through Earth's oceans for longer
than trees have existed. Their ancient ancestors appeared
hundreds of millions of years before humans.

Fossil evidence indicates that early sharks existed more than
400 million years ago. The earliest known trees appeared
later, around 385 million years ago.

Although modern sharks have evolved considerably since then,
their ancient history makes them one of the oldest surviving
animal lineages. They've even outlasted the dinosaurs!
explanation:
TRUE! Fossils date early shark
ancestors to before the earliest
known trees. Museum and fossil
records can confirm the timeline.
This doesn't mean modern sharks
never evolved.

title: Music Makes Plants Grow Twice as Fast
author: Isabella Hayes
text:
A gardening website claims that playing pop music to plants
can double their growth rate. The article recommends placing
speakers beside gardens for at least an hour each day.

The researchers supposedly tested several groups of plants
and found that those listening to music grew much faster.
The website suggests that certain songs work better than others.

However, the article provides no information about the number
of plants tested, their growing conditions or whether the
experiment was reviewed by independent scientists.
explanation:
FAKE! No sample size, growing
conditions or published study are
provided. Plant responses to
vibration don't prove pop music
doubles growth. Look for
controlled experiments.

title: Wombats Produce Cube-Shaped Poo
author: Hannah Cooper
text:
Australia is home to many unusual animals, but wombats have
one particularly strange talent: producing cube-shaped poo.
Yes, actual cubes, and no, they don't use tiny moulds.

Scientists have investigated how this happens and found that
different levels of stiffness and stretching inside the
wombat's intestines help shape the waste before it leaves.

The unusual shape may help the poo remain in place when wombats
use it to mark their territory. Unlike round droppings, cubes
are less likely to roll away from rocks and logs.
explanation:
TRUE! Researchers have examined
how wombat intestines form
cube-shaped droppings. The claim
sounds silly, but scientific
studies and wildlife sources can
verify it.
